definition: A Neural Network Gaussian Process (NNGP) is a Gaussian process (GP) obtained as the limit of a certain type of sequence of neural networks.
details: Specifically, a wide variety of network architectures converges to a GP in the infinitely wide limit, in the sense of distribution. The concept constitutes an intensional definition, i.e., a NNGP is just a GP, but distinguished by how it is obtained.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. And that shape of the machine — Neural network Gaussian process — is what makes everything else possible.
